source: Why, my lord, of course she did. She overheard my men and I discussing it. Of course, I am the true source of this information.
I see. Very well, then. It merely gave me a nasty surprise, to have her walk up to me and assert something of that nature.
Lady Ophelia was the one who delivered me promising information about Prince Fortinbras hiding out nearby.
This is not a new possibility to me, of course. But she presented her case most convincingly.
More of this Prince Fortinbras business. An eminent thorn in my side, that one.
My lord, I have learned—not only does Fortinbras intend to betray his peacetime agreement with us, he intends to stage a coup.
The Prince and his men are, at this very moment, hiding out in town, just outside the castle gates. They intend to lay siege to us by Sunday.
Oh, not all this again. I understand that none of us are used to trusting Norway, but they are our allies now. We must keep the faith.
Hasty moves have lost us many a battle in the past.
I fully believe it now. The fool has overextended himself and crossed a line which cannot be uncrossed.
Still, hasty moves here have lost us many a battle in the past.
Prince Fortinbras has no intentions beyond our lands. He wants to take the Danish throne. His request to cross Danish lands is a ruse.
He hides out now, in town, with a small group of officers.
Sir, perhaps this is a time to reiterate... I've long believed Prince Fortinbras has no intentions beyond our lands. He wants to take the Danish throne.
You finally believe me, my lord?
I do. And I give you suitable permission to act.
My lord, I beg of you. Something like this should be simple to verify.
Allow me to take my men into town. If all is as we believe it to be, we will come away with Prince Fortinbras as prisoner.
And if not, there will be nothing to fear. We can frame it as a routine investigation of the town's seedier alleyways.
There can be no harm in investigating.
So be it. Keep your profile low.
Of course, my lord, of course.
And one last thing. If you come away empty-handed...
There shall be no more talk of pulling peace agreements with Norway. Now, or evermore.
This sort of thing has the power to grow from rumor to dangerous absolute if we do not either confirm it or hinder it at the knees.
Yes, my lord. If this town investigation bears no fruit, I think that's wise.
Then we may need to pursue further action. I'm convinced Fortinbras means to act against us somehow. We simply haven't identified the method yet.
Let us be done with this, then.
Thank goodness. It sounds like everyone's collectively come to their senses.
Bernardo and his men should mobilize soon. Here's hoping they find Fortinbras.
Then there won't be a coup.
Men, follow me.
Wot's all this about, Captain?
We're operating on a special request from the King, to find Prince Fortinbras.
We have recent cause to believe the Prince is hiding out in town.
P-P-Prince Fortinbras?!
Why, that lyin', connivin' dog...
This will take the form of an ordinary sweep. Raise no alarm, and mention nothing of our business.
If we do find him, bringing him under arrest is our first priority.
And if we find nothing, it is the King's desire that we give the townspeople nothing to fear.
Aye, Captain.
Given the turmoil within Elsinore, I don't feel right leaving the court unprotected—so we'll be rather light for this endeavor.
Are the five o' us enough? What if Fortinbras 'as men of 'is own?
It's certainly not an ideal staffing scenario. But we must do what we must do.
(This doesn't seem promising.)
The five of us will lead the initial foray, but the rest of the Castle Guard will be swift to follow.
I'm confident that we're well-staffed to handle this endeavor. We'll quickly overtake whatever cohort Fortinbras has.
Aye, captain!
Let's have at it!
Knock on every door.
If the occupants refuse, force entry.
We found somethin'!
Who are you?
Marcellus. Remove his hood.
As I thought. You are the singular Prince Fortinbras.
And you are here with the intent of usurping the King of Denmark.
Indeed. I came to do what my father could not.
You came ill-prepared and undermanned, I see.
An ambush?
We can't hold them off, Captain!
They're retreating—
They were deflected, but—the Prince escaped, no doubt to whatever rathole they maintain.
We failed.
We should report these events to the King.
...We were short, m'lord. We knew it wos a risky move.
Aye. Had we not left men back in Elsinore, we might have prevailed today.
Had all been peaceful within the castle, then perhaps...
But there's no sense waxing philosophical about what might have been.
Our failure here was absolute, and I must acknowledge it to everyone.
You killed my finest officers. Good men of large standing.
I know not how you found us, but it would appear I have been summarily outmatched.
We received a tip from Lady Ophelia here. She knew you would be in town.
I have heard tell of this Lady Ophelia before. Who is she?
I'm the one you were going to have killed. Not anymore.
Men, take him to the dungeon. I shall work with the King on how best to proceed.
Well! What have the dogs sniffed out now?
A hare in our trap! And a fat one, at that.
Young Prince Fortinbras. Welcome to Elsinore.
Had I but one more day, our positions would have been exchanged here, Denmark.
Yes, well, you didn't, and they aren't.
What shall I do with you now? Perhaps write to your uncle and ransom you back in chains?
That old man Norway, impotent and bedridden. He doesn't know about this deceit of yours, does he?
Yes. I will use you to re-fill Denmark's coffers, and secure a true peace between us.
But not just yet, I think.
First, I think I'll let you enjoy the darkness and the silence a little while.
Perhaps Bernardo can give you a turn on the rack. Or a little carving to remember us by.
(My lord, is that wise?)
Mmm, perhaps not. But neither was this coup of the Prince's. I'm only having a little fun.
Regardless, the day is won. This battle goes to Denmark.
Sweet dreams, my dear Prince.
We must uncover a way to communicate this checkmate to all in Elsinore.
At once, Your Highness. As soon as we're prepared to make an announcement, let us do so.
That's the herald's horn.
Bernardo and the King are preparing to make a statement about Fortinbras, I expect. I should attend.
This is an unusual time for an announcement. I ought to go see.
This is an unusual time for an announcement.
My apologies for the sudden disturbance, my lords and ladies.
I bring to you some sudden news.
My men and I learned earlier of a Norwegian plot to overthrow His Majesty and bring about the subjugation of Denmark.
Prince Fortinbras aimed to violate his peacetime agreement with us in the name of bloody revenge.
However, thanks to some well-timed information, we were able to stop him in his tracks and bring him under arrest.
He's now safely contained in Elsinore's dungeon, down in the casemates.
Does this mean peace?
Is the war with Norway at an end?
Does this mean peace for us, at last?
I have never known a longtime peace in Elsinore.
Does this mean peace for Denmark at last?
What happens now?
Why, we'll make a show of force to old King Norway, bedridden back home!
Send his nephew home in chains. Show him what happens to unruly boys who cannot learn to act with civility.
Regrettably, I remain unconvinced this is the end of anything.
This is merely the beginning.
I do not believe Prince Fortinbras has any intentions of relenting. The wise thing to do would be to execute him as an enemy of the state.
However, were we to do so, we would invoke the wrath of his uncle, the King of Norway.
There is no simple solution. All this is but a temporary peace.
Thanks to some well-timed information, we were able to intercept the Prince in town and drive him off.
We... had hoped to capture him. But recent losses have stretched our forces thin, it seems. He escaped our grasp.
Still--whatever he was planning has been delayed, at least.
(With any luck, this has brought me enough time to meet Simona.)
Let us prepare for a longer fight.
I leave it in your hands, Bernardo.
I'll have word sent to rally all troops who would hear the call.
Until then, everyone, please remain vigilant.
So? Now what, my lord?
Both of us in a birdcage.
Hmph. Far from it.
Don't fret, Lady Birgitta.
I haven't given up hope on returning to my men. This court is already fraying, I can see it. If any piece falls, we'll have our chance.
I have other loyal agents. All they need is an excuse to act.
I'm less optimistic.
Lady Birgitta.
My lord!
How did they discover my location? Did you--
Of course not! But you were imprisoned. The other men had no clarity of action behind them.
I'm certain they'll rally regardless.
Without you, they won't accomplish anything against Elsinore. They're scattered. Frightened. They needed you.
Perhaps they shall have me yet. This court is already fraying, I can see it. If any piece falls from the board, we'll have our chance.
If there is but a moment of chaos...
Then I—or one of your officers—must come here to free you. I understand.
('If any piece falls.')
(I need to keep them all alive.)
(No one must die. I can save them. I have to.)
Ah, my captain. It's good to see your face.
I never doubted you would come for me.
The King's untimely death has brought them all together... and left you unkept, my lord.
The Queen's untimely death has brought them all together... and left you unkept, my lord.
The young Prince's untimely death has brought them all together... and left you unkept, my lord.
The old Master Chamberlain's untimely death has brought them all together... and left you unkept, my lord.
Lord Laertes' untimely death has brought them all together... and left you unkept, my lord.
Let their chaos be our convenience.
Come, Your Highness. I'll return you to the gates.
Come, Your Highness. We'll get you to the gates.
Let's make haste. I'm not sure how long Bernardo's men will let down their guard.
I have failed in my duties most utterly.
